definition: Preclude means to prevent something from happening — to make it impossible in advance.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word preclude. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know preclude should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: A clause in her contract precludes her from working for a competitor for two full years.
To hinder something is only to slow it down — it can still happen. To preclude it is to shut the door on it entirely, before it can even start.
A ban adds force and authority on top of what preclude does: something is formally forbidden, with penalties for anyone who tries anyway.

Prevent is the everyday, all-purpose word for keeping something from happening — a fence prevents accidents. Preclude is its formal relative with a sharper edge: something is made impossible in advance, shut off before it can even start, and it appears mostly in legal and official prose. Anything precluded is prevented, but preclude insists the door never opened at all.

To bar something is to block it by rule or authority — a person or institution does the barring: the league bars ineligible players. Preclude works impersonally: a schedule conflict or an injury can preclude something with no authority involved. Bar needs someone wielding a rule; preclude needs only circumstances that close the door.

To rule out is to eliminate a possibility, usually by deciding or reasoning — a doctor rules out one diagnosis, a planner rules out a venue. Someone weighs an option and strikes it from the list. Preclude does the striking without anyone deciding: conditions themselves make the thing impossible in advance.

Preclude means to prevent something from happening — to make it impossible in advance.
Because the two required classes meet at exactly the same hour, taking chemistry this semester precludes taking orchestra.
The schedule conflict doesn't merely make orchestra harder — it shuts off the possibility entirely, in advance.
That is the force of preclude: the door is closed before you ever reach it.
Preclude appears mostly in legal, academic, and official prose: a rule precludes an action, or precludes someone from doing something.
It signals true impossibility, not mere discouragement — if bad weather merely makes a picnic unpleasant, it hasn't precluded it.

Astronomers spent four years searching for a home for the Halden infrared telescope, and water vapor did most of the eliminating.
Moisture in the air absorbs infrared light before it reaches any mirror, however large.
A humid site would therefore preclude the very observations the telescope was built for — not hamper them, but shut them off entirely, in advance.
